hypothesis:
The MLP expansion ratio has never been varied. `4 * config.n_embd` appears exactly twice per file in all 432 nodes of this campaign -- the ratio is hardcoded and has been constant since trial one, while depth (8/10/11/12/13/14), aspect ratio (36/39/42/51/64) and head dim (64/128/256) were all explored. It is the largest untouched structural axis in the model.

It matters most now, for two reasons. The MLP holds roughly 25M of the ~46M non-value-embedding parameters and is the model's biggest FLOPs consumer, so its width trades capacity against step count almost directly under a fixed 300-second budget. And the trade is now measurable: t0433 just demonstrated that throughput converts to bpb exactly as the token law predicts, with a +1.14% step gain producing -0.000494 against a predicted -0.000662 and a mechanism residual of +0.000168, inside the floor. So a width change can be decomposed cleanly into the throughput it buys or costs and the capacity it loses or gains, which is precisely the decomposition this campaign is equipped to make and has never had an untouched axis to apply it to.

This arm narrows the MLP to 3x. It removes about 6.3M parameters and a corresponding slice of per-step FLOPs, which should buy a step increase several times larger than the +1.14% that just took the championship. The bet is that this model is over-provisioned in MLP width relative to what a 300-second budget can train: the campaign's own history supports that reading, since depth 13 and 14 both lost while depth 12 held, which is the same capacity-versus-steps trade in a different dimension.
change_summary: A new MLP_RATIO = 3 constant, and both `4 * config.n_embd` sites in the MLP class now read `MLP_RATIO * config.n_embd`. Per-layer hidden width goes 2048 -> 1536. Nothing else changes: same depth, same residual width, same attention, same optimizer groups. The edit asserts exactly two occurrences exist and that MLP_RATIO is not already present, and refuses ratio 4 as a no-op. Dry-run against the t0433 champion source patched both sites and parsed.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
Both terms move and in opposite directions, so I am registering the arithmetic rather than a single number. Throughput should rise -- if steps go up by x, the token law credits -0.0586*ln(1+x). Capacity should fall, and that debit has no prior in this campaign because the axis is untested. If the measured delta is more negative than the throughput credit alone, capacity was not binding and 3x is better than 4x. If it is less negative, capacity is binding and the two effects can be separated numerically for the first time on this axis.
Unlike almost every other trial, a large step change here is EXPECTED and is the mechanism, not contention. I will only treat a step change as contention if it is inconsistent with the parameter count removed.
risk:
This is a large change and could lose badly; a narrower MLP may simply be worse at any step count. I accept that because a clean loss still measures the capacity term on a virgin axis, which is worth more than another null on a saturated one.
The interpretive risk I want to guard against: if this wins, the temptation is to read 'narrow the MLP' as a direction and keep going to 2x. Two points do not make a direction -- that is the extrapolation error this campaign has made three times -- which is why the 5x arm is queued behind this one regardless of what this returns. Bracketing is what closed the warmdown axis honestly and it is what should close this one.
